$comment: Registry of substrate the platform has RETIRED. Consumed by
scripts/check-retired-substrate.mjs, which FORBIDS the terms below in every
tracked file except the closed lists in this file.
Why this exists: when BET-5 retired Neo4j and Qdrant onto PostgreSQL, the
code changed and the words did not. /architecture/platform-overview/ kept
describing Neo4j as a live service, the disaster-recovery runbook kept telling
operators mid-incident to restore a database that no longer exists, and config,
prompts, compose files and dead code kept naming it for months. Nothing failed,
because no gate was watching the words.
historicalRoots: path prefixes that are records of the past and are never
rewritten (dated plans and specs, immutable migrations, evidence). Each carries
its reason.
allowed: the only other files that may name a retired term, each with the
reason the mention is still true or still load-bearing. The list is CLOSED and
only shrinks: a file not listed here fails, and an entry whose file no longer
names a retired term fails as stale until it is removed. Do not add an entry
for a mention you cannot honestly call history, a guard, or third-party data;
a live instruction pointing at a dead service is a defect, not debt.
TO RETIRE SOMETHING: add a `retired` entry, run `pnpm check:retired-substrate`,
and fix every file it lists. Expect a long list the first time; that list is
the blast radius you would otherwise have shipped past.

retired.replacement: the Postgres graph mirror — graph_node / graph_edge, traversed in packages/db/src/pg-graph.ts

historicalRoots.docs/superpowers/: Dated plans and specs are the design record of their day; they are superseded, never rewritten.
historicalRoots.packages/db/prisma/migrations/: Migrations are forward-only and immutable after commit (AGENTS.md section 2).
historicalRoots.benchmarks/bet5-datastore/: The BET-5 parity benchmarks against live Neo4j and Qdrant: the evidence the retirement was decided on.
historicalRoots.changes/: Per-PR data-impact records and exceptions, frozen at the change they describe.
